avalancheActivity.comment: In the highest elevations of the High Tatras, the Western Tatras, and the highest elevations of the western part of the Low Tatras, a low avalanche danger—Level 1—persists above the 1,800-meter elevation. This is primarily due to wind-drifted snow on the leeward sides (east and southeast) of the highest elevations. Be cautious in very steep areas, narrow gullies, and notches where snow accumulates. Here, due to precipitation combined with strong winds, small snow slabs and snow pillows may form on leeward slopes. Light snowfall and strong winds are still expected throughout the day, especially in the morning. Prolonged low temperatures and a thin snowpack are major factors contributing to the formation of hazardous snow types within the snowpack.
avalancheActivity.highlights: Watch out for drifted snow on leeward slopes (E, SE). Watch out for prolonged low temperatures and thin snow cover.

snowpackStructure.comment: Following the passage of a cold front, a cold air mass has moved into the mountainous regions of Slovakia, and cold Arctic air will continue to flow into these areas throughout Monday. We expect snow showers and continued strong winds during the day. Continuous snow cover begins at 1,500 meters above sea level. Due to low temperatures, the snow remains powdery and, at the highest elevations, lies on top of an old, hard snowpack. These two layers are not sufficiently bonded and form a dangerous layer prone to detachment—especially under additional load. Prolonged low temperatures favor the formation of dangerous snow grain types in the snow profile. The thickness of the new snow layer may vary depending on the aspect, but averages 20–30 cm.

tendency.highlights: With expected precipitation and low temperatures, the risk is increasing.
